mainEntity.name: Can a cosmetic claim to treat acne?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not in the US, where acne treatment claims make it an OTC drug. Cosmetic claims focus on blemish-prone skin, the appearance of blemishes and shine.

mainEntity.name: Does makeup make acne worse?

acceptedAnswer.text: A controlled study found makeup did not slow acne improvement and improved quality of life. We design non-comedogenic textures and test them.

mainEntity.name: How do you test a non-comedogenic claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a comedogenicity assessment on panels, and in-use studies on blemish-prone skin.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the formula?

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to formulate a cosmetic product?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the product type, the number of actives, the claims and the markets. After a short brief call we give a fixed quote for formulation, and separate quotes for testing and regulatory work so you only pay for what you need.

mainEntity.name: How long does cosmetic product development take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full project typically takes 21 to 36 weeks from brief to pilot batch. Stability testing and claims studies usually set the pace, and projects that start with an existing formula are shorter.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from me to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: A short brief: product type, target consumer, a benchmark if you have one, the claims you want, your markets, pack and target price. See the checklist on How we work.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will you reply?

acceptedAnswer.text: A scientist replies within one working day with next steps and an indicative scope.

mainEntity.name: Do you sign an NDA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, before you share your brief or formula.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with startups?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many first-time founders come to us with an idea and a price point. See the Startups page.

mainEntity.name: How do you price projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fixed fees per stage, agreed in a written proposal. No hidden costs for sample rounds included in the proposal.

mainEntity.name: What is the MOQ?

acceptedAnswer.text: Micro-batches are sized to your requirement. There is no factory MOQ.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do.

mainEntity.name: Can I move production to another manufacturer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We provide a full tech-transfer pack.

mainEntity.name: How long does a new product take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typically 5–9 months from brief to launch-ready, depending on testing, claims and markets. Use the timeline calculator on How we work.

mainEntity.name: How long does stability testing take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Accelerated stability gives a first read at about 12 weeks; real-time studies continue to confirm shelf life.

mainEntity.name: Can testing run in parallel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Claims studies and regulatory preparation usually run alongside stability testing.

mainEntity.name: What does “dermatologically tested” require?

acceptedAnswer.text: At minimum a dermatologist-supervised patch test or in-use study on the final formula. See the claim finder.

mainEntity.name: Do you test on animals?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We use validated in vitro methods, ingredient safety data and supervised human studies.

mainEntity.name: What is a challenge test?

acceptedAnswer.text: A preservative efficacy test to ISO 11930 showing the product resists contamination during use.

mainEntity.name: Can you test SPF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes: in vivo SPF to ISO 24444, UVA to ISO 24443 and PA rating to ISO 24442.

mainEntity.name: Can you act as our EU or UK Responsible Person?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, through an EU- or UK-established legal entity named in your agreement.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to register under MoCRA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most brands selling in the US must register facilities and list products. Some small businesses are exempt. Read our MoCRA guide.

mainEntity.name: Can one safety assessment cover several markets?

acceptedAnswer.text: An EU-format CPSR is the strongest base; we add market-specific documents.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide Free Sale Certificates?

acceptedAnswer.text: We prepare the documents needed to obtain Free Sale Certificates and other export papers.

mainEntity.name: Is a CPSR mandatory for cosmetics sold in the EU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Article 10 requires a safety assessment and a CPSR for every cosmetic before it is placed on the market. The Responsible Person keeps it in the Product Information File.

mainEntity.name: Who can sign an EU CPSR?

acceptedAnswer.text: A safety assessor holding a diploma or other evidence of formal qualifications from a university course in pharmacy, toxicology, medicine or a similar discipline, or a course recognised as equivalent by a Member State (Article 10(2)).

mainEntity.name: What Margin of Safety is acceptable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under the SCCS Notes of Guidance, a MoS of at least 100 is generally considered to indicate safe use for an ingredient that reaches the systemic circulation.

mainEntity.name: Does a CPSR need updating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Update it whenever the formula, a supplier, the annexes or undesirable-effect data change. A CSL compliance retainer covers this file maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Are natural oils safe for newborns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. Some plant oils can affect the developing skin barrier. We choose and test oils rather than assume they are gentle.

mainEntity.name: How are baby products tested?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but usually as two variants. In the US a dandruff claim makes it an OTC drug with a permitted active, while in the EU it is a cosmetic and zinc pyrithione is no longer allowed. We plan the active and claims for each market from the start.

mainEntity.name: Can a cosmetic claim to stop hair loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not in most markets. Cosmetics can claim to reduce hair fall due to breakage, reduce shedding or give denser-looking hair. Claims to regrow hair or treat alopecia make the product a medicine.

mainEntity.name: Can you develop hair supplements as well as topical products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Through our group we develop nutricosmetic supplements, such as marine protein or botanical formulas, alongside topical products, each with the right regulatory route.

mainEntity.name: How do you prove a hair repair claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: We start with instrumental tests on hair tresses (tensile strength, breakage, combing force, frizz imaging) and then confirm the result in an in-use study on consumers.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the hair care formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. We sign an NDA before you share your brief, and the formula and technical file are handed over at the end of the project.

mainEntity.name: Is there a fee to join the supplier directory?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Listing is free for qualified suppliers.

mainEntity.name: Is the directory public?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is used by our formulation, sourcing and project teams to select materials for client projects.

mainEntity.name: How long does qualification take?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the category and the documents you provide. Most suppliers with complete documentation are reviewed within a few weeks.

mainEntity.name: Do you guarantee orders?
